chunks: The Obligations (legislated shares of inheritance) and divorce cannot be established except by the sword.

key_terms.السَّيْفُ: The sword — a metonym for legitimate political and judicial authority, particularly the Imam's governing power to enforce legal rulings.
key_terms.الطَّلَاقُ: Divorce — the formal dissolution of marriage. In Islamic law, divorce has specific procedural requirements to be legally valid.
key_terms.الْفَرَائِضُ: The obligatory shares — Quranic term for divinely mandated inheritance portions (Quran 4:11-12). The plural fara'id refers to the enforced distribution of estates according to Islamic law.

ai.seo_question: Can inheritance distribution and divorce be enacted without legitimate Islamic authority according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (AS) declares that two major legal institutions — the division of inheritance according to the divine apportionments (fara'id) and the pronouncement of divorce — cannot be properly enacted without legitimate governmental authority, symbolized by 'the sword.' In Shia jurisprudence, this statement reflects the doctrine that certain legal acts require the presence or authorization of the just Imam, as without legitimate authority, legal rights may be violated. The original audience, living under unjust Umayyad rule, would have understood this as a reminder that proper legal order is tied to the rightful Imam's authority.
